info.title: ShieldTX Partner API
info.description: HTTP contract for the ShieldTX server-managed wallet integration. Every operation requires a current Privy user access token. Partner requests use a JWT issued for the registered partner app. The saved account connection survives JWT expiry; expired JWTs are rejected. The hosted ShieldTX window uses a ShieldTX user JWT plus the verified linked account hint, except /connect, which verifies both user tokens. Partner app secrets and private authorization keys are not used by this API. Requests and responses use JSON unless a framework error states otherwise. Request bodies are limited to 100000 bytes. When an Origin header is present it must match the caller app's registered origin. Writes are asynchronous where documented; acceptance is not proof of a fill or returned funds. Request budgets are 6000 calls per partner per 60-second window, with per-account budgets of 3 combined connect/setup calls and 120 other calls per 60-second window. Retry HTTP 429 with backoff and preserve request IDs.

get.description: Returns configuration for the authenticated partner. Authentication is required. Use authAppOrigin as the trusted origin for the ShieldTX window and use the returned network and contract addresses together.

Returns the authenticated account connection, setup readiness, up to 200 wallets and 100 recent trades. Before connection, connection and nsRoot are null and setupReady is false. Poll for asynchronous progress. Disconnect leaves account and accepted-trade status readable.

Returns a JSON string containing spendable USDC. Requires an active connection and initialized Nightshade read session. Polling needs only the partner user token and does not request signatures. HTTP 409 READ_SESSION_REQUIRED requires explicit renewal through the ShieldTX window. A missing session or read failure is never reported as zero. The read session is retained for at most 12 hours and can expire sooner at the sequencer.

post.description: Called by the ShieldTX window after the user approves. Send the ShieldTX user JWT in Authorization and the partner user JWT, including its Bearer prefix, in X-Stratium-Authorization. Both tokens are independently verified. nsAddress must be the ShieldTX user's embedded Solana wallet. The saved partner user, ShieldTX identity and root cannot be replaced; reconnect must use the same identities and root. Returns HTTP 409 CONNECTION_CONFLICT for conflicting bindings. When Origin is present, it must be the registered ShieldTX origin.

Revokes new setup, wallet replenishment and trade admission, and clears the retained read session. Accepted trades continue and authenticated close/return operations remain available. Signing out does not revoke this connection. Accepts an empty body or {}.

Requires an active saved connection. Provisions fixed policies, recipient sets and empty wallet pairs. A pair contains a position EVM wallet, relay EVM wallet and relay Solana wallet. Prewarming moves no funds. Retry an interrupted request using the same requestId and walletCount. A completed batch returns replay true. A different count for an existing ID returns REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT. SETUP_RECONCILE_REQUIRED needs operator reconciliation; using a new ID does not resolve an unknown resource-creation outcome. Wait for available wallets with active revocation state before opening a trade. The server also maintains wallet inventory automatically. Raw policies, owners and recipient overrides are not accepted.

get.summary: Find an order by request ID
get.description: Exact lookup scoped to the authenticated account, including orders older than the recent-trades snapshot. Returns order null when no matching order is visible. Use this endpoint to reconcile an uncertain open before signing another funding intent. reshieldStage is null in this lookup; poll GET /account for return progress.

parameters.name: clientOrderId
parameters.description: The original open request idempotency key.

post.summary: Submit a signed funding request and open a trade
post.description: Requires executionEnabled, an active connection and completed wallet setup. The ShieldTX window obtains user approval and prepares the signed Nightshade CreateIntent request. The API verifies the linked root signature and binds the signed recipient, expected funding amount and solver sender to the request. Use the configured solver and USDC asset when constructing the intent. HTTP 202 acknowledges admission, not a Hyperliquid fill. Follow GET /account or GET /orders/{clientOrderId}. Retrying an identical request under the same clientOrderId returns the existing trade with replay true. Reusing an ID with different request contents returns a conflict. Preserve the identical signed request for retries; if it is lost, reconcile the exact order before building another intent. The example signature and read token are placeholders and must be replaced with current values.

post.summary: Close a full position or cancel an eligible pending trade
post.description: Closes the full position for a trade owned by the caller. An eligible funded trade that has not entered may instead be cancelled. Partial closes and client-supplied wallet, pair or size overrides are not accepted. nsOwnerAccount must equal the linked root. Reuse clientOrderId when retrying. HTTP 202 is acceptance; replay true indicates an already accepted close or cancellation. Close and return access remain available after disconnect for accepted trades.

post.summary: Request or resume the return of trade proceeds
post.description: Queues a return request for a trade owned by the caller. HTTP 202 means enqueued only; eligibility and return processing continue asynchronously. Repeat requests use the same tradeId; execution resumes from recorded progress. Poll GET /account for reshieldStage and GET /balance for spendable returned funds. This endpoint remains available after disconnect for accepted trades.

Low-level read transport used by the ShieldTX signing window. Send only method and params; the coordinator creates the JSON-RPC envelope. Supported methods are getLimits, getChallenge, getAuthToken and getUnspentNotes. Public keys must match the linked root. A successful getAuthToken result initializes the retained balance session for an active connection. The sequencer response is returned unchanged, so an HTTP 200 response can contain a JSON-RPC error. getUnspentNotes uses an item offset starting_index; advance by the returned page length until an empty page. Tokens, notes and signatures are sensitive; the partner balance endpoint exposes only the total.

Called only by the ShieldTX window with ShieldTX authentication and X-ShieldTX-Account-Id. Records diagnostic signing events; reports do not establish authoritative billing. id identifies the event and operationId correlates the signing operation. This endpoint is not part of partner frontend onboarding.

post.description: Burns the input notes and queues an L1 withdrawal of `amount` to `l1_recipient`; any remainder stays shielded as a change note. Sent to the sequencer once and never retried. HTTP 502 UNSHIELD_UNCONFIRMED is ambiguous: check history before signing again (resending the same body is harmless). The withdrawal becomes claimable after the next proven batch, typically up to about two hours.

post.description: Returns one page (up to 10) of the owner's unshields, oldest first; an empty page ends the list. Advance startingIndex by the number of records received. HTTP 409 READ_TOKEN_REJECTED means the read token expired and must be signed again. Rate-limited per owner.

PartnerAccessToken.description: Current user access token issued by privy.io for the registered partner app. Signature, audience, issuer and timestamps are verified.

ShieldTxAccessToken.description: Current user access token issued for the ShieldTX Privy app. Used by the hosted ShieldTX window.

ShieldTxAccountId.name: X-ShieldTX-Account-Id
ShieldTxAccountId.description: Linked account UUID. Required with ShieldTX authentication outside /connect. It is a routing hint, not a credential; the verified ShieldTX owner must match the saved connection.

PartnerConnectionToken.name: X-Stratium-Authorization
PartnerConnectionToken.description: The full string Bearer <partner-user-access-token>. Used together with a ShieldTX Authorization bearer token only for /connect.

NonzeroUuid.description: UUID used for an account, trade or idempotency key. The nil UUID is not accepted for write request IDs.

SolanaAddress.description: Base58-encoded embedded Solana public key. Must belong to the authenticated ShieldTX user.

Decimal.description: Base-10 decimal string; use strings to preserve precision.

PositiveDecimal.description: Strictly positive decimal string. Zero and negative values are rejected.

MicroUsdc.description: Positive integer string in atomic USDC units (1 USDC = 1000000).

U256Quantity.description: Unsigned 256-bit integer encoded as a hexadecimal quantity or decimal string.

f.description: Builder fee in tenths of a basis point; 10 means 1 basis point.

executionEnabled.description: Whether new trade execution is enabled for this partner.

authAppOrigin.description: Approved origin of the hosted ShieldTX login and signing window.

warmTarget.description: Target inventory of ready wallet pairs.

walletLimit.description: Lifetime wallet-pair creation cap for an account.

nsRoot.description: Immutable linked Nightshade owner public key.

status.description: Wallet availability. Select only available wallets for a new trade.

relay.description: True for an EVM relay wallet; false for a position wallet.

revocationState.description: A usable wallet must have active revocation state.

stage.description: Durable execution stage. A failed or successful terminalStatus is separate from this stage.

anyOf.description: Return progress. The exact-order lookup does not join return progress and returns null here; use GET /account for this field.

wallets.description: Up to 200 most recently created position and EVM relay wallets.

trades.description: Up to 100 most recent trades. Use GET /orders/{clientOrderId} for an exact lookup outside this window.

setupReady.description: Provisioning readiness. Check active connection and individual wallet availability before starting a trade.

Balance.description: Spendable shielded USDC, with up to six decimal places. Zero is a valid successful balance; read failures use an error response.

nsAddress.description: Base58 form of the already-linked ShieldTX Nightshade root.

requestId.description: Stable request ID. Retry the same ID and wallet count after a temporary failure.

walletCount.description: Number of new wallet pairs. Each pair has a position EVM wallet, relay EVM wallet and relay Solana wallet.

timeout_blocks.description: Intent timeout measured in L1 blocks.

input_commitments.description: Commitments of the funding notes. The configured sequencer input-note limit applies.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature by nsOwnerAccount over the canonical Nightshade intent hash. JSON examples contain placeholder bytes, not executable signatures.

clientOrderId.description: Stable idempotency key scoped to the authenticated partner user.

dexPositionAccount.description: Available position wallet selected from this account. The signed intent must fund this exact wallet.

pair.description: Market symbol. Availability is checked during execution.

leverage.description: Positive integer; supported leverage depends on the Hyperliquid market.

sizeUsd.description: Position notional in USD, not margin. Must be covered by the signed funding amount and leverage.

nsOwnerAccount.description: Must equal the immutable linked Nightshade root.

sequencerReadAuthTokenHex.description: Current sequencer read token for this root. Request-scoped sensitive value.

clientOrderId.description: Stable close request ID. Reuse for retries.

nsOwnerAccount.description: Return owner; must match the linked Nightshade root.

operationId.description: Correlation ID for the signing operation.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. Handle codes rather than matching message text.

message.description: Human-readable description; not a stable identifier.

retryable.description: A retry may succeed. This does not prove that a timed-out operation had no effect. Preserve request IDs and reconcile uncertain writes.

ReadResponse.description: The sequencer JSON-RPC response, including JSON-RPC errors under HTTP 200. A getLimits result is SequencerLimits; getChallenge and getAuthToken return Bytes32; getUnspentNotes returns Note[].

UnshieldRequest.description: A SignedTransaction whose payload is Unshield, signed by the owner of every input note. The ShieldTX window builds and signs it.

authToken.description: Sequencer read token from getChallenge/getAuthToken signed by publicKey.

id.description: Vault leaf hash of the unshield; stable identifier and the value Vault.processedUnshields is keyed by.

BadRequest.description: Invalid fields, root or signed funding request. Malformed path parameters may use a framework plain-text error.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired Privy token. Obtain a current token before retrying.

error.message: invalid or expired Privy access token

Forbidden.description: Origin, wallet ownership, linked root or active connection check failed.

error.message: funding owner must match your registered NS root

NotFound.description: Trade does not exist or belongs to another account.

Conflict.description: Account, setup, read session or trade state requires reconciliation or another action.

error.message: Refresh your ShieldTX read session to resume balance updates

RateLimited.description: Request budget exceeded. Back off and retry the same request ID.

BadGateway.description: Privy or the Nightshade sequencer is unavailable.

Unavailable.description: Execution is disabled, capacity is busy or a required service is unavailable.

error.message: opens disabled until test funding infrastructure is ready

PayloadTooLarge.description: Request exceeds the 100000-byte HTTP body limit. Framework-generated errors may use plain text instead of the JSON error envelope.

UnexpectedHttpError.description: Other HTTP or framework failures may use a different response body, including plain text.
